title: DROP ZONE: RENEGADE HARDWARE
content:
[gallery type="rectangular" ids="466,467,468,469,470,471,472,473,474,475,476,477"]

Drop Zones second label night featured none other than the heavyweight champion of murky DnB: Renegade Hardware. Unfortunately, after two decades of history, an unforgettable back catalog of amazing releases and epic events, the pioneering label will close down permanently. Despite that Drop Zone gave them and the Finnish drum and bass following the farewell it deserves; An unforgettable night with the legendary artists Doc Scott, BTK and Maztek, not forgetting a hefty Finnish support line up. Influential, not influenced. Future beats, for future people. Renegade Hardware, gone but never forgotten.

Long live drum and bass!

title: Kumarachi ‘’Hold It Down'' EP
content:
Kumarwho? Kumarwhat? Funny as his name is (a combination of his surname and liberace) I've had my eye and ear on this Nottingham based producer for at least a year or two, and couldn't resist doing a spotlight on this up and coming diamond in the rock deep inside the jungle/drum and bass scene. From releases like Phatty, Droid Ting (a tune seriously underrated and a personal favorite) and Badman Ting VIP, his production and versatility in sound has significantly caught my attention in this time, and as a result we proudly present a full review of his newest EP ‘’Hold It Down’’ on DJ Hybrids Audio Addict Recordings As we hold it down here in Helsinki, we kick off the session with the first tune, in collaboration with DJ Hybrid (who won producer of the year in the ‘’we love jungle’’ awards btw), it's time to get down and dirty.

‘’Hold It down’’ starts off innocent and sweet; melodic and filtered soundscapes complimented with a lovely female vocal ‘’hold me’’, slowly building up to juicily layered drums that quickly warp into a kick drum build up and perfectly timed drum fill, ‘’hold it down’’ erupts like a volcano into a huge magmatic bassline and bongo ride, as the vocal switches in between a male ‘’yeah’’ and the original ‘’hold me’’, keeping you on your feet till the second drop. You can definitely hear the best of both producers in this one, full of energy and very well thought through. I specifically like the bongo ride and reggae tin pan drum roll on this one. From innocent to pure tearout, you can definitely hear these guys aren't messing about!

 Time to send for the new gun! Although we don't encourage or support any sort of violence by any means, ‘’send for dem’’ is a militant tune without a doubt. Starting off with a likkle gun talk and vicious oldschool piano stabs (he does play piano you know), jumpy drums and a cheeky reverse gun talk drop off vox, it's time to set off C4 and obliterate the dancefloor with this one. The chainsaw reece bassline is all over the place, taking you to different dimensions, whist giving time for echoed ragga vocals and some very cheeky drum switch ups and with that creeping oldschool piano slowly coming in, this tune is absolutely making a statement of Kumarachi’s versatility in his music production. Let's take it back. Way back. Listen to the hypnotic pads, cold and fresh soundscapes, filtered drums filled and a soothing vocal, from the intro of ‘’love box return’’. It oozes with soul, passion and one hell of a punch. The intro is very reminiscent of early 94 jungle, with great manipulation of the break, ‘’love box return’’ does a whole 360 degree turn and makes you screw up your face whether you like it or not. Like chuck norris it roundhouse kicks you in the back of the neck with a next level bassline and intelligent drum programming, and Kumarachi’s trademark percussion (I wonder if he plays drums too?). This tune is definitely for the pinnacle of the party, however giving the right amount of space for the ravers to chill and take a deep breath. As the legend himself put it: ‘’I don't initiate violence, I retaliate’’ C.N Time to get grimey. ‘’1013’’ starts off like it's coming straight from the gutter, with proper sinister sewer pipeline grooves, very reminiscent to the UK Grime sound, massive dem better buckle up and settle in cause this one is filthy. Surprising you with a huge rise and ultra punchy build up, ‘1013’’ guarantees any raver to raise their gunfinger in the air and shout ‘’bust it up’’, no sorry ‘’pull it up’’. As the deep rolling bassline glides along each bassbin and frequency , carrying a very sinister synth stab and heavy bongo madness, this one hits you like a ton of bricks, and will leave you feeling like you've been up all weekend, finally getting home to eat whatever is left in the cupboard, which is dry weetabix, and the milkman ain't even been yet. As stated, grimey like a limey without a cuppa in the morning. Blimey.

 ‘’Junglist Styles’’ Going back to my reference of the versatility of Kumarachis production, this is a prime example. Delayed, filtered  and clean intro sounds with a lovely DJ friendly hat/maraca  shaker, plus an an acute bass stab coming out of nowhere, Junglist styles really shows the full potential of this producer. Rare groove is the essence and foundation of this tune in my opinion, again, guilty until proven innocent, this one rolls out till the very end. With a delayed vox, we infiltrate one of the biggest jungle roller drops to date, full of perfect drum percs, cymbals, ridiculous bass switches and a lovely claves clap combination throughout, all in all, this is a true jungle riddim.

 ‘’Dont Go’’ is my personal pick of the EP, slowly building up with very ravey yet authentic oldschool elements, the pads gradually elevating deliberately with a sensitive bleep synth, and lovely hat tease it gives you just a millisecond to realise what the hell is going on. Out of nowhere comes Kumarachis own imprint (insane!) bassline breakbeat pressure rinseout, with some tidy yet tastefully mangled vox and pure attention to detail. I think he really went back to his roots on this one, and it has a sound that makes me feel like i'm travelling through the solar system, whilst being rotated around an asteroid belt at warp speed. If I could describe it to a fellow junglist or junglette, I would use the term ‘’97 dope dragon on redbull with a naughty junglematical twist’’ . But let's not get too specific, fact of the matter is, this one's a banger and you know it. One for the intro, one for the last raver standing, one for the Kepler crew, this one's you. With support from some of the biggest DJ/Producers  in the game, including Ray Keith, Kenny Ken, Dazee, Jaybee, AshAtack, Lion Dub, Random Movement and of course yours truly, this release is definitely worth checking out! Keep an eye and an ear out for Kumarachi in the future, if he keeps releasing tunes like this it's only a matter of time that he’ll be playing at a venue near you! Like the tunes? Check out the full purchasable EP here! More about audio addict here!

title: Drop Zone Critical Label night
content: With an array of bookings from one of the most respected electronic music labels in the UK, in a brand new location and backed up by the kind of stunningly impressive visual work by Matlock visuals that we have come to expect from a Drop Zone party, what more could you ask? Rising from the underground, Drop Zone pushes the cutting edge soundscapes of past, present and future. Their first club event was all about Critical Music with guests Kasra, Enei and Hyroglifics. In the future we will see Drop Zone with both club and underground events, more info here! [gallery type="rectangular" ids="408,418,409,417,413,420,407,414,412,415,411,410"]

title: Kallio Block Party 2015
content:
The first of August Kallio's Katri Vala park became the stage for a couple of thousand spectators who felt the bass vibrations for a whopping eight hours. Ivah Sound System had their setup in full with a custom made stack of speakers to make the whole block shake. It was a truly mesmerizing experience, with both old and young united with each other enjoying the sound system in the sun.
"This is exactly why we made Ivah Sound in the first place, to bring people together with the power of music and love. Huge respect to Paleface for delivering his set with a deep and conscious message regarding peace, unity and power to the people, not forgetting the thousands of you who came to experience Ivah Sound System throughout the day. This is something we will all remember for a long time." - Ivah Sound
The Helsinki based crew have been active for over five years, taking the sound system culture of Finland forward. The foundation of Ivah Sound's music comes from a Jamaican descent although the sound has a large variation of selections and styles ranging from roots all the way to jungle and steppas. title: Helsinki Underground w/ Mr Explicit
content:
Norwich born Mr Explicit or “The Scientist” as they call him at Dread Recordings, joined the Dread camp around five years ago with the massive tune “Dark Assassin”, three incredible Vinyl EPs later and his latest remix is of “Dark soldier” coming out soon and it's going to be huge! Mr Explicit has proved himself to be a very talented producer, his biggest track “Cringe” a huge anthem and a favourite of the drum and bass elite. Mr Explicit was heavily influenced from the early Jungle, Garage and Hardcore scene and started to produce in 2005 where he met Ray Keith who together with Bladerunner nurtured the young raw talent right up to his first few releases. It's looking very promising in 2015 for Explicit, with vicious rumors going around of releases from Ash Attacks Label, Directors Cut (under his and Venom’s joint venture project Undercover Audio) Bryan G’s Philly Blunt and of course Ray Keith’s Dread Recordings to name a few. We are very honoured to have him in Finland for the first time. So buckle up your seat belts and saddle in cause it's going to get Explicit! Attached you can find a very special studio dub mix from Mr Explicit himself, featuring mostly all of his newest production from 2015 and the highly sought for remixes of the stone cold antherm "Dillinja - Motherfucka" and "Ed Rush & Optical - Cutslo". He asked us a couple of weeks ago what kind of set he should bring and we said absolutely everything goes, so he's literally been making all sorts of styles of drum and bass in the studio just for his gig here in Helsinki. So we can't emphasise enough how stoked we are for having him over! Check out the event here!

MR Explicit 2015 Studio Mix by Trey on Mixcloud

title: Drop Zone
content: [gallery type="rectangular" ids="260,259,257,256,254,251,246,242"] Welcome to the underground scene of the small capital city of Finland; Helsinki. It's time to enter the Drop Zone. At first glance, this seems like a small scale festival around an industrial area located close to an old power plant. But we assure you this is not the case. The scene is familiar, old friends, new faces, new friends, old faces, no matter how many times these parties reoccur, there is always something exceptional about the support regarding the scene. A fusion of bass music fanatics, both new comers and old heads which makes the atmosphere truly unique. Organization is always a tough job, especially on a scale like this. But Drop Zone is an underground movement that has organized many successful parties like this in the past, and this time it's no different, the crew outdid themselves once again. The big hall started off with deep trap vibes, followed by Grime and a live performance from Axel Thesleff. When the live performance comes to an end its time for drum and bass. Fanu steps up on the ones and twos and the crowd have been aching for some breakbeat pressure all night. Starting off with some classic jungle techno from the likes of Dillinja, Baby B Kane and of course Fanus own slow fast trademark remixes and reworks, its time to call out to all the jungle warriors. With lazers flashing, ravers raving, sound system pumping and people jumping it's time for the rudeboy ragga muffin headliner; Alix Perez. Alix is known for his versatile production and remarkable DJ skills which were evident throughout his set at Drop Zone. We were lucky enough to have a front row seat as a MC and photographer combination to witness this spectacle. Giving Helsinki a run for its money, Perez demolishes the huge crowd with exclusive material, continuous technical double drops, genre switch ups, rewinds and not forgetting relicks of classic "remember the rollers" bladerunner remix. With every style of drum and bass covered throughout the night with finesse and professionalism it's safe to say that if we were living in 1996 you would definitely be buying a tape pack of the night from your local record shop. Room two was strictly for the steppers, dim lights and deep mediation vibrations provided by dubstep pioneers Sub Root. All in all Drop Zone was a full audio visual experience, an array of domestic and international DJ's with the dancefloor packed it goes without saying that bass music has found an indefinite future in the underground of Helsinki.

title: Musical Murderation
content: No war business, seen! Well, actually in this case there is war business, but war of the musical sort. Its a square off between two top Jungle producers Habitat & The Force. Lets have a little look and listen to the ammunition these guys have been cooking up in their studios.       As we square off, the first tune of the EP is from Habitat, titled See Me Coming This Hip Hop dagger is an extremely playful two step riddim, laced with funky horns, maraca shakers and a uber bouncy bassline with rolling drums to keep your feet moving, definitely one for the one foot skankers. See me coming, start running, for cover that is... As we move on to the second tune of the EP , The Force proceeds to retaliate with City Love. Straight from the intro you can already hear The Force's trademark uplifting oldschool pads complimented with energetic drums and a soulful female vocal. With a tight build up, the tune drops into a deep rolling bass that would do damage to any decent soundsystem.   Tied at 1-1, we enter sudden death. The Force goes in with Musical War. With a dubby and eerie intro packed with dancehall soundscapes,  a very beautiful melodica stab build up, Musical War drops with a huge ten tonne bassline. This one reminded me of a revamped Commix classic ''Be True'' with a lovely dubby touch. Musical murderation indeed!   As MC Bassman says, ''sharp like a razor, cut you, make you bleed'' and this one does exactly that! Habitat goes all out with this absolutely filthy ragga jungle warhead. With a timestreched vocal ''razor blade'' dropping into bass switches, jungle drum fills and dub sirens, you would be mad not to pull this one up instantly.   With the war over and the dust settled, I can't honestly decide which one of the producers won the war. However the two stand out tracks from this EP for me are Musical War and Razor Blade. All in all another fantastic release from the Bristol based label Ruffneck Ting, definitely one to look out for in 2015. You can buy this EP release exclusively at Juno here

title: Paradox in Helsinki
content: [gallery type="rectangular" ids="36,71,72,73"] ‘’Live’’ Its a term thrown around a lot in the electronic music scene. Even more so in the drum’n’bass scene. Its a broad term, meaning something possibly with a live band, PA performance of a tune straight out the studio to just a sampler and/or drum machine played live by the music producer. With that said, we get a first hand glance of the master of live drum and bass, for the first time ‘’playing’’ in Finland; Paradox. As you enter the venue you can already hear the booming sounds of finnish young guns Meraki warming up the dancefloor back to back with deeper shades of drum and bass. As the people start flowing through the doors, the atmosphere intensifies and you can already say the vibe is electric. There is certainly an essence of jungle in the air. Around quarter past twelve the dancefloor is packed and Helsinki Jungle Mafia DJ Physics steps up on the decks alongside their resident MC Cypha. With a versatile set packed with dancefloor rollers, stone cold classics and forthcoming dubplates from his album Long Road LP Cypha activates the ravers with familiar hooks and crowd hype. While a fresh remix of Lennie D Ice’s ‘’We Are Ie’’ is playing you can see Paradox on stage at his mixing desk preparing floppy discs for his set. As Physics and Cypha rinse out the last one, its time for the headliner. Paradox quickly introduces himself and proceeds to go into full focus behind his mixing desk. In a nutshell, he’s live, in his studio, making music for the masses. Amen after amen, break after break and bassline after bassline, he hosts his set flawlessly, explaining what's going on and what's coming in next in each interval - Paradox in full effect. Outside, there is a fusion of international drum and bass heads, local junglists and first timers on the scene. With a perfect delivery of both old and new, Paradox gives an outro speech and ends his set. The vibes are still rolling and the ravers are still skanking as Burma and Cypha take the stage. For the last hour its upfront rolling drum and bass with a couple of exclusive dubplates from Burmas joint venture project Random Heroes. As the energy is still oozing at half past three, its a wrap! You can catch the next Helsinki Jungle Mafia event on the 15th of May in Helsinki.

title: Skating w/ Manny
content:
[gallery type="rectangular" size="medium" ids="58"]

When Trey lived in a small spanish village in the Valencia region (circa 2003) surrounded by non english speakers, the only means of communication he had was his skateboard. He had just learned 360 flips while skateboarding in Finland, so naturally the locals started calling him by the name Trey. The name stuck and had a ring to it so later he incorporated it as his DJ alias and hasn't looked back since.

Also, the Eight Trey Gangsta Crips is a Los Angeles latino gang, although born in California and having latino roots, Trey has no known affiliation with the Crip sub division. You can catch Trey Tre flipping around the streets of Helsinki with a smile on his face.

title: About
content: Top Shelf is a drum & bass collective consisting of two members; Prospero and Trey. They first started actively DJ’ing around 2011 and have come a long way since. Both driven by the love of drum & bass, they decided to put their heads together to bring you a combination of styles and selections. Ranging from deep dark and dirty, raggamuffin jungle slammers, all the way to liquid rolling bliss. Expect full energy sets, back to back madness, and a full spectrum of all drum & bass styles and exclusive material from Finland and all around the world. Contact: topshelf(a)ivahsound.com

title: Ivah Sound system
content: [gallery type="rectangular" size="medium" ids="123"] Ivah Sound is a sound system and DJ collective formed in Helsinki during early 2010. United by a common passion for heavy bass music they play styles ranging all the way from roots reggae to steppers, jungle and drum & bass. The two main Junglists Prospero and Trey met in the early years of the sound system and later established their own drum & bass collective Top Shelf. The sound system is constructed by the best of Finnish birch wood and only using high quality components. Building the sound system themselves was always a clear choice as it is a large part of the sound system culture itself.

title: FRWRD - a sound system club
content: [gallery type="rectangular" size="medium" ids="101,103,102,104,356"] FRWRD - a sound system club brought to you by Ivah Sound, made for passionate bass music and sound system lovers. With influences from the sound system cultures of Jamaica and The United Kingdom they combine music with a heavyweight sound. FRWRD brings the party to a crowd hungry for mesmerizing experiences with performers both from Finland and abroad.
